chunks: And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: One who makes a believer happy has in fact made me happy; and one who makes me happy has in fact made Allah happy.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for making a believer happy according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), articulates the theological concept of *ittisal* (connection) where the pleasure of the common believer serves as a direct conduit to the pleasure of the Prophet and ultimately God. In Shia scholarship, this underscores the ontological status of the *Ummah* as the locus of divine satisfaction, reinforcing the ethical imperative of *ihsan* (beneficence) towards fellow believers as an act of worship. It highlights that social kindness is not merely moral but a spiritual mechanism for attaining divine proximity.
